sentences.zh: 略兄新蔡武哀王騰

translations.literal: Lue's elder brother Prince Wuai of Xincai Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Lue's elder brother Sima Teng, Prince Wuai of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 新蔡武哀王騰，字元邁，少拜冗從僕射，封東嬴公，曆南陽、魏郡太守，所在稱職，徵為宗正，遷太常，轉持節、寧北將軍、都督并州諸軍事、并州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince Wuai of Xincai Teng courtesy Yuanmai in youth was appointed supernumerary chariot master and enfeoffed Duke of Dongying; successively governor of Nanyang and Wei commandery where he was praised competent; summoned Grand Director of the Imperial Clan; promoted Minister of Ceremonies; transferred credential-bearing Pacifying North General supervising Bing military affairs and Bing Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng, Prince Wuai of Xincai, courtesy name Yuanmai, was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant when young and enfeoffed as Duke of Dongying. He served successively as governor of Nanyang and Wei Commandery, was praised as competent wherever he served, was summoned as Director of the Imperial Clan, promoted to Minister of Ceremonies, and then transferred as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, commander of all military affairs in Bing Province, and inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 惠帝討成都王穎，六軍敗績。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned against Prince of Chengdu Ying the six armies were routed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's expedition against Sima Ying collapsed.

sentences.zh: 騰與安北將軍王浚共殺穎所署幽州刺史和演，率眾討穎。

translations.literal: Teng together with Pacifying North General Wang Jun jointly killed Inspector of You appointed by Ying—He Yan—and led hosts against Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Teng joined Wang Jun executing He Yan then marched on Ying.

sentences.zh: 穎遣北中郎將王斌距戰，浚率鮮卑騎擊斌，騰為後系，大破之。

translations.literal: Ying dispatched Northern Gentlemen General Wang Bin to resist; Jun led Xianbei horse striking Bin while Teng covered the rear routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei cavalry under Wang Jun shattered Wang Bin while Teng held the rear.

sentences.zh: 穎懼，挾帝歸洛陽，進騰位安北將軍。

translations.literal: Ying feared and escorted the emperor back to Luoyang; Teng was advanced Pacifying North General.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was afraid and took Emperor Hui back to Luoyang; Teng was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，遷車騎將軍，都督鄴城守諸軍事，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: Early Yongjia he was promoted chariot-and-cavalry general supervising Ye garrison stationed at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia named him chariot-and-cavalry chief at Ye.

sentences.zh: 又以迎駕之勳，改封新蔡王。

translations.literal: Again for merit welcoming the imperial carriage his enfeoffment was changed Prince of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the throne earned the Xincai princedom.

sentences.zh: 初，騰發并州，次於真定。

translations.literal: At first when Teng set out from Bing Province he halted at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Bing he paused at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 值大雪，平地數尺，營門前方數丈雪融不積，騰怪而掘之，得玉馬，高尺許，表獻之。

translations.literal: It happened there was great snow several chi deep on level ground; before the camp gate several zhang of ground showed melted snow not accumulating; Teng wondered and dug obtaining a jade horse about a chi high which he memorialized and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Snow melted oddly at his gate; digging revealed a jade horse sent to court.

sentences.zh: 其後公師籓與平陽人汲桑等為群盜，起於清河鄃縣，眾千餘人，寇頓丘，以葬成都王穎為辭，載穎主而行，與張泓故將李豐等將攻鄴。

translations.literal: Later duke-lord Shi Fan with Pingyang men Ji Sang and others formed bandit gangs rising in Shu county of Qinghe over one thousand strong raiding Dunqiu using burying Prince of Chengdu Ying as pretext loading Ying's spirit tablet marching with Zhang Hong's old general Li Feng intending to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang's gang marched under Ying's tablet to threaten Ye.

sentences.zh: 騰曰：「孤在并州七年，胡圍城不能克。

translations.literal: Teng said, 'I was at Bing seven years and barbarians besieging the city could not overcome it.
translations.idiomatic: Teng said, 'I was at Bing seven years and barbarians besieging the city could not overcome it.

sentences.zh: 汲桑小賊，何足憂也。」

translations.literal: Ji Sang petty bandits—what worth worry.'
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang petty bandits—what worth worry.'

sentences.zh: 及豐等至，騰不能守，率輕騎而走，為豐所害。

translations.literal: When Feng and others arrived Teng could not defend and led light horse fleeing and was killed by Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The raid overwhelmed him; fleeing lightly armed he fell to Feng.

sentences.zh: 四子：虞、矯、紹、確。

translations.literal: Four sons: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons survived: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que.

sentences.zh: 虞有勇力，騰之被害，虞逐豐，豐投水而死。

translations.literal: Yu had courage and strength; when Teng was harmed Yu pursued Feng who threw himself in water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu avenged his father driving Feng into the river.

sentences.zh: 是日，虞及矯、紹並钜鹿太守崔曼、車騎長史羊恆、從事中郎蔡克等又為豐餘黨所害，及諸名家流移依鄴者，死亡並盡。

translations.literal: That same day Yu together with Jiao and Shao and Julu governor Cui Man chariot-and-cavalry chief clerk Yang Heng consultant Cai Ke were again harmed by Feng's remaining faction and renowned families taking refuge at Ye perished altogether.
translations.idiomatic: The bloodbath wiped Julu officials and refugee clans at Ye.

sentences.zh: 初，鄴中雖府庫虛竭，而騰資用甚饒。

translations.literal: At first though Ye granaries were exhausted Teng's private wealth was very ample.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's arsenals stood empty yet Teng hoarded wealth.

sentences.zh: 性儉嗇，無所振惠，臨急，乃賜將士米可數升，帛各丈尺，是以人不為用，遂致於禍。

translations.literal: By nature stingy he showed no generosity; facing crisis he then gifted officers several sheng of rice and bolts only one zhang therefore men would not serve him and ruin followed.
translations.idiomatic: His miserly handfuls of grain and cloth bought no loyalty and brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 及苟晞救鄴，桑還平陽。

translations.literal: When Gou Xi relieved Ye Sang returned to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi's relief sent Ji Sang back toward Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 于時盛夏，屍爛壞不可復識，騰及三子骸骨不獲。

translations.literal: It was then deep summer; corpses rotted beyond recognition and Teng's and his three sons' bones could not be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: It was midsummer, and the corpses had decayed beyond recognition; the remains of Teng and his three sons could not be recovered.

sentences.zh: 庶子確立。

translations.literal: His son by a secondary consort, Que, succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son by a secondary consort, Sima Que, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 莊王確，字嗣安，曆東中郎將、都督豫州諸軍事，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang Que, courtesy name Si'an, successively served as General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the East and supervised the military affairs of Yu Province, stationed at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Que, Prince Zhuang, styled Si'an, successively served as General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the East and supervised the military affairs of Yu Province, stationed at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，為石勒所害。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia he was harmed by Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le killed him at Yongjia's close.

sentences.zh: 無子，初以章武王混子滔奉其祀，其後復以汝南威王祐子弼為確後。

translations.literal: He had no sons. At first Tao, son of Hun, Prince of Zhangwu, was appointed to maintain his sacrifices; afterward Bi, son of You, Prince Wei of Runan, was made Que's heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons. At first Tao, son of Hun, Prince of Zhangwu, was appointed to maintain his sacrifices; afterward Bi, son of You, Prince Wei of Runan, was made Que's heir.

sentences.zh: 太興元年薨，無子，又以弼弟邈嗣確，位至侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixing, Bi died without sons. His younger brother Miao was then made Que's successor and rose to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taixing, Bi died without sons. His younger brother Miao was then made Que's successor and rose to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 薨，子晃立，拜散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He died; son Huang succeeded appointed irregular cavalry gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Huang inherited as supernumerary cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 桓溫廢武陵王，免晃為庶人，徙衡陽。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen deposed Prince of Wuling Huang was degraded commoner and banished Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's coup reduced Huang to commoner exile in Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝立晃弟崇繼邈後，為奴所害，子惠立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu enthroned Huang's younger brother Chong continued Miao's line and was harmed by slaves; son Hui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Chong continued Miao yet fell to household slaves; Hui followed.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song accepted the abdication the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song ended the fief.

sentences.zh: 略弟南陽王模

translations.literal: Younger brother of Lue Mo Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang—Lue's brother.
